world.title: Estonia accuses Russia of ordering Tallinn defense-company arson
world.summary: Estonia said on Sept. 29 that its Internal Security Service had concluded that Russian special services ordered an arson attack on a building used by Milrem Robotics in Tallinn on the night of Aug. 14-15. The company makes unmanned ground vehicles, including THeMIS systems used by Ukraine. Firefighters quickly extingui
world.content: Estonia said on Sept. 29 that its Internal Security Service had concluded that Russian special services ordered an arson attack on a building used by Milrem Robotics in Tallinn on the night of Aug. 14-15. The company makes unmanned ground vehicles, including THeMIS systems used by Ukraine. Firefighters quickly extinguished the blaze, and no one was injured. Prime Minister Kristen Michal said the finding followed the security service’s assessment of gathered intelligence. Authorities withheld supporting evidence, citing the confidential nature of the information, and said the criminal investigation was continuing. Three Latvian suspects were transferred to Estonia, which summoned Russia’s chargé d’affaires. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov rejected the accusation as baseless, while NATO and EU officials voiced support for Estonia.
world.image_alt: Estonia accuses Russia of ordering Tallinn defense-company arson

world.title: Netanyahu warns of pre-election attack; Lapid challenges claim
world.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Tuesday, Sept. 29, that there were indications Israel’s enemies might attack before the Oct. 27 general election. In a video filmed at Tel Nof Airbase, he did not name a potential attacker or disclose details of the intelligence behind the warning. Opposition leader Yair L
world.content: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Tuesday, Sept. 29, that there were indications Israel’s enemies might attack before the Oct. 27 general election. In a video filmed at Tel Nof Airbase, he did not name a potential attacker or disclose details of the intelligence behind the warning. Opposition leader Yair Lapid sought an urgent security briefing and met Netanyahu later that day. Lapid accused Netanyahu of stoking fear, said the election should proceed on schedule and cited intelligence failures before Hamas’s Oct. 7, 2023, attack.

world.title: Eiffel Tower operator chief to step down after exclusion of female staff
world.summary: Patrick Branco Ruivo, director general of the company operating the Eiffel Tower, will leave his post at the end of 2026 after an investigation found that planning failures led to female employees being excluded during a Sept. 5 visit by a delegation linked to the Hindu organization BAPS. The group, in Paris for the op
world.content: Patrick Branco Ruivo, director general of the company operating the Eiffel Tower, will leave his post at the end of 2026 after an investigation found that planning failures led to female employees being excluded during a Sept. 5 visit by a delegation linked to the Hindu organization BAPS. The group, in Paris for the opening of a temple, numbered about 100 people; some female staff were replaced by male colleagues. Employees went on strike on Sept. 7, closing the tower for a day. The operator said BAPS had asked for arrangements to limit interactions with women and that it should not have accepted the request; its investigation called the resulting exclusion unacceptable.
world.image_alt: Eiffel Tower operator chief to step down after exclusion of female staff

world.title: UK police find petrol, no explosives near US airbase
world.summary: British counterterrorism police reported Tuesday that searches of three vans linked to five suspects arrested near RAF Fairford found no improvised explosive devices but recovered a quantity of petrol. Police said military resources and forensic experts assisted with the examination. The five men, British nationals in
world.content: British counterterrorism police reported Tuesday that searches of three vans linked to five suspects arrested near RAF Fairford found no improvised explosive devices but recovered a quantity of petrol. Police said military resources and forensic experts assisted with the examination. The five men, British nationals in their 20s, were arrested Sunday on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences and released on bail Monday; they remain under investigation. Investigators are examining multiple lines of inquiry, including whether the suspects had links to Iran. Iran has denied involvement. RAF Fairford is used by U.S. forces, including in operations against Iran.
world.image_alt: UK police find petrol, no explosives near US airbase

world.title: Israeli settlers block court-ordered return of Palestinian family
world.summary: More than 100 Israeli settlers attacked Jalud in the occupied West Bank overnight from Monday to Tuesday as Israeli forces tried to escort the Tubasi family back to their homes. The military said settlers blocked roads, set fires, threw rocks at security forces, and burned Palestinian homes and vehicles; three Border P
world.content: More than 100 Israeli settlers attacked Jalud in the occupied West Bank overnight from Monday to Tuesday as Israeli forces tried to escort the Tubasi family back to their homes. The military said settlers blocked roads, set fires, threw rocks at security forces, and burned Palestinian homes and vehicles; three Border Police officers were lightly injured. Police said one person was arrested and two minors were questioned, while the military said the violence halted the return operation. The family left Jalud in July after repeated settler harassment, and Israel’s High Court ordered authorities earlier in September to enable its return. The family could not remain in their homes after the attack.
world.image_alt: Israeli settlers block court-ordered return of Palestinian family

world.title: French high school protests bring 440 detentions nationwide
world.summary: French authorities detained 440 people, most of them minors, during nationwide high school protests on Tuesday, Sept. 29. Students demonstrated over overcrowded classes, teacher shortages, long timetables and poor school conditions. The movement began around Paris and spread to cities across France. Officials reported
world.content: French authorities detained 440 people, most of them minors, during nationwide high school protests on Tuesday, Sept. 29. Students demonstrated over overcrowded classes, teacher shortages, long timetables and poor school conditions. The movement began around Paris and spread to cities across France. Officials reported injuries to 48 law-enforcement officers, at least 10 teachers and several students. Some protests escalated into clashes: students set rubbish bins on fire and threw objects at police, who used tear gas. The demonstrations coincided with a public-sector strike over proposed government budget cuts, two days before Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu was due to present the 2027 draft budget.
world.image_alt: French high school protests bring 440 detentions nationwide

world.title: UN Command says North Korean DMZ mine breached armistice
world.summary: A joint investigation by the United Nations Command and the South Korean military concluded that a mine blast in the Demilitarized Zone violated the Korean War armistice. Explosions on Sept. 21 injured three South Korean personnel during a reconnaissance mission; two were seriously injured. South Korea demanded that Py
world.content: A joint investigation by the United Nations Command and the South Korean military concluded that a mine blast in the Demilitarized Zone violated the Korean War armistice. Explosions on Sept. 21 injured three South Korean personnel during a reconnaissance mission; two were seriously injured. South Korea demanded that Pyongyang apologize and take responsible measures, urged it to halt border fortification, and said it would take measures in stages. North Korea denied planting the mines. Kim Yo Jong, the North Korean leader’s sister, called Seoul’s findings fabricated and warned of retaliation if South Korean forces fired on North Korean troops.
world.image_alt: UN Command says North Korean DMZ mine breached armistice

world.title: Supreme Court lets Trump resume third-country deportations
world.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court on Sept. 29 temporarily allowed President Donald Trump’s administration to resume deporting migrants to countries other than their own without first giving them a chance to challenge the destination based on possible harm. The 6-3 order granted the Justice Department’s emergency request to pause
world.content: The U.S. Supreme Court on Sept. 29 temporarily allowed President Donald Trump’s administration to resume deporting migrants to countries other than their own without first giving them a chance to challenge the destination based on possible harm. The 6-3 order granted the Justice Department’s emergency request to pause a lower-court ruling that had blocked the policy; it does not settle whether the policy is legal. The court scheduled oral arguments for December on the policy’s legality and related questions, with a final ruling to follow. Human rights groups say more than 25,000 migrants have been sent to 29 countries since the policy began in 2025, with the vast majority sent to Mexico.
world.image_alt: Supreme Court lets Trump resume third-country deportations

business.title: Trump weighs diesel export ban as fuel prices surge
business.summary: Fuel prices are rising ahead of the midterm elections, prompting White House discussions about possible restrictions on U.S. diesel exports. No policy decision had been made as of Sept. 29. The administration says the aim is to lower domestic fuel costs; Trump acknowledged that an export curb could also raise gasoline
business.content: Fuel prices are rising ahead of the midterm elections, prompting White House discussions about possible restrictions on U.S. diesel exports. No policy decision had been made as of Sept. 29. The administration says the aim is to lower domestic fuel costs; Trump acknowledged that an export curb could also raise gasoline prices. The debate follows a surge in fuel prices linked to disrupted global supplies during the Iran conflict and Russia’s war in Ukraine. U.S. diesel prices were near a record average of $6.45 per gallon, according to AAA.
business.image_alt: Trump weighs diesel export ban as fuel prices surge

business.content: Disney is laying off about 300 employees, mainly in human resources and technology, in its latest workforce reduction under CEO Josh D’Amaro. In its August earnings report, Disney identified labor reductions as one of several cost-control measures under review. The cuts mark the third round since D’Amaro became CEO in March.

business.title: Middle East oil exports recover as prices stay elevated
business.summary: Middle Eastern crude shipments rebounded in September as Saudi Arabia restored flows through its East-West pipeline and more oil moved through the Strait of Hormuz. Bloomberg, citing JPMorgan analysts, said the region’s 10-day average exports reached 17.5 million barrels a day, or 98% of pre-war levels. Separately, pre
business.content: Middle Eastern crude shipments rebounded in September as Saudi Arabia restored flows through its East-West pipeline and more oil moved through the Strait of Hormuz. Bloomberg, citing JPMorgan analysts, said the region’s 10-day average exports reached 17.5 million barrels a day, or 98% of pre-war levels. Separately, preliminary Kpler data put September exports from major regional producers at 16.3 million barrels a day, below February’s 19.5 million. The New York Times reported that global oil supply remained below demand. Oil prices eased on Sept. 30 following a sharp drop in the previous session, with Brent near $96 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate around $90, Bloomberg reported. Prices remained elevated as shipments still faced disruption and some exports relied on costlier ship-to-ship transfers. Analysts also cited continuing geopolitical risk around the strait.
business.image_alt: Middle East oil exports recover as prices stay elevated

business.title: French debt reaches 119% of GDP as borrowing costs rise
business.summary: France’s public debt reached €3,595.5 billion at the end of June, equal to 119% of GDP and up €59.6 billion from the previous quarter, according to Insee. The ratio was the highest recorded since 1946. The debt total had already risen by €75.8 billion in the first quarter. The government is due to present its 2027 budg
business.content: France’s public debt reached €3,595.5 billion at the end of June, equal to 119% of GDP and up €59.6 billion from the previous quarter, according to Insee. The ratio was the highest recorded since 1946. The debt total had already risen by €75.8 billion in the first quarter. The government is due to present its 2027 budget on Thursday, reportedly proposing €54 billion in savings and targeting a deficit of 5% of GDP. The government expects debt to reach 121.7% of GDP in 2027, when France plans to issue a record €340 billion in bonds. Higher borrowing costs and pressure on public finances prompted Vanguard to warn of “degrading credit”.
business.image_alt: French debt reaches 119% of GDP as borrowing costs rise

business.title: Alaska and Hawaiian plan premium cabin overhaul for 2028
business.summary: Alaska Air Group said on Sept. 29 it will overhaul premium cabins on Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines, adding lie-flat suites and a new Premium Reserve premium-economy class. The company said the changes are part of its effort to compete for premium customers. The new Alaska Aurora suites are planned for Boeing 78
business.content: Alaska Air Group said on Sept. 29 it will overhaul premium cabins on Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines, adding lie-flat suites and a new Premium Reserve premium-economy class. The company said the changes are part of its effort to compete for premium customers. The new Alaska Aurora suites are planned for Boeing 787s and some 737 MAX 10s, while Hawaiian will add Leihōkū suites to its A330 fleet. Cabin changes are expected to begin rolling out in 2028.
business.image_alt: Alaska and Hawaiian plan premium cabin overhaul for 2028

business.title: U.S. consumer confidence falls to lowest level since 2014
business.summary: U.S. consumer confidence fell 6.7 points in September to 81.9, its lowest reading since April 2014 and below its pandemic-era low, the Conference Board said Tuesday. The index stood at 88.6 in August. Respondents cited high prices for goods and services, including gasoline and oil, as well as concerns about wages and j
business.content: U.S. consumer confidence fell 6.7 points in September to 81.9, its lowest reading since April 2014 and below its pandemic-era low, the Conference Board said Tuesday. The index stood at 88.6 in August. Respondents cited high prices for goods and services, including gasoline and oil, as well as concerns about wages and jobs. The survey was conducted from Sept. 1 through Sept. 23. The Iran war pushed up fuel costs while inflation remained elevated. The Conference Board’s Dana Peterson said consumers’ assessments of current business conditions turned negative for the first time since September 2024. The confidence reading also fell short of the 89.2 economists forecast in a Reuters poll.
business.image_alt: U.S. consumer confidence falls to lowest level since 2014

business.title: Smart ring maker Oura postpones $2.2 billion IPO
business.summary: Oura, the Finnish-founded smart-ring company, postponed its Nasdaq IPO on Sept. 29, citing uncertainty in the new-issue market despite strong investor demand. It had planned to offer 50 million shares at $40 to $44 each, seeking as much as $2.2 billion. The offering included 13.5 million new shares and 36.5 million sha
business.content: Oura, the Finnish-founded smart-ring company, postponed its Nasdaq IPO on Sept. 29, citing uncertainty in the new-issue market despite strong investor demand. It had planned to offer 50 million shares at $40 to $44 each, seeking as much as $2.2 billion. The offering included 13.5 million new shares and 36.5 million shares sold by existing investors. Oura has not announced a new listing date. The transaction was intended mainly to allow some existing shareholders to sell holdings rather than raise new funding for Oura’s expansion. Renaissance Capital cited concerns about slower artificial-intelligence spending, renewed Federal Reserve rate hikes and rising bond yields as factors weighing on IPO activity.
business.image_alt: Smart ring maker Oura postpones $2.2 billion IPO

business.title: Trump and six tech leaders sign voluntary AI safety pact
business.summary: President Donald Trump and executives from Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, Nvidia and xAI signed a voluntary White House accord on Sept. 29 covering safeguards for advanced AI systems. The commitments call for company controls, internal monitoring, independent external audits and board-level review. Trump rejected cal
business.content: President Donald Trump and executives from Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, Nvidia and xAI signed a voluntary White House accord on Sept. 29 covering safeguards for advanced AI systems. The commitments call for company controls, internal monitoring, independent external audits and board-level review. Trump rejected calls for new federal restrictions on AI development and said companies should police their own systems. He also signed an executive order renaming artificial intelligence as “Superintelligence”.
business.image_alt: Trump and six tech leaders sign voluntary AI safety pact

Those fans also reported lower intentions to take climate-friendly actions, the researchers said.
science.content: A study published in the journal Psychology of Popular Media found that young adults who strongly identified as Taylor Swift fans were more likely to justify her private-jet emissions after reading about them. Those fans also reported lower intentions to take climate-friendly actions, the researchers said.

science.summary: The John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation announced its 2026 fellowship class on Sept. 29, naming 20 people across disciplines. Each fellow will receive an unrestricted $800,000 award. Among those recognized is forensic anthropologist Kate Spradley, whose work involves identifying and repatriating migrants’ rem
science.content: The John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation announced its 2026 fellowship class on Sept. 29, naming 20 people across disciplines. Each fellow will receive an unrestricted $800,000 award. Among those recognized is forensic anthropologist Kate Spradley, whose work involves identifying and repatriating migrants’ remains. Other fellows include researchers in climate and energy policy, agriculture and theoretical physics.
science.image_alt: MacArthur names 20 fellows, including science and justice researchers

science.title: Researchers urge study of poorly explored Antarctic ice basin
science.summary: Researchers from 14 countries have called for a coordinated international campaign to study East Antarctica’s largely unexplored Wilkes Subglacial Basin, which contains enough ice to raise global sea levels by three to four metres if it melted. The basin lies mostly within Australia’s Antarctic Territory. Researchers s
science.content: Researchers from 14 countries have called for a coordinated international campaign to study East Antarctica’s largely unexplored Wilkes Subglacial Basin, which contains enough ice to raise global sea levels by three to four metres if it melted. The basin lies mostly within Australia’s Antarctic Territory. Researchers say evidence from past warm periods indicates substantial retreat, but current data are too sparse to establish what conditions could trigger large-scale melting. The basin spans about 1,400 kilometres by 400 kilometres.

science.title: Scientists report seven of nine planetary boundaries breached
science.summary: More than 60 scientists wrote the Planetary Health Check 2026, which reports that seven of nine planetary boundaries have been breached. The report says Earth faces an increasing risk of irreversible harm as the window for action closes.
science.content: More than 60 scientists wrote the Planetary Health Check 2026, which reports that seven of nine planetary boundaries have been breached. The report says Earth faces an increasing risk of irreversible harm as the window for action closes.

science.title: Moon and sun may trigger slow earthquakes through resonance
science.summary: A model study published in JGR: Solid Earth proposes that periodic gravitational stresses from the moon and sun can trigger slow earthquakes when their timing matches a fault’s response, a process analogous to pushing a swing in rhythm. The study addresses a longstanding question about how the small stresses associated
science.content: A model study published in JGR: Solid Earth proposes that periodic gravitational stresses from the moon and sun can trigger slow earthquakes when their timing matches a fault’s response, a process analogous to pushing a swing in rhythm. The study addresses a longstanding question about how the small stresses associated with these celestial bodies can initiate fault movement. Slow earthquakes release energy gradually rather than in the abrupt motion associated with ordinary quakes, and people cannot feel them, Tuoi Tre reported.
science.image_alt: Moon and sun may trigger slow earthquakes through resonance

science.title: Hurricane Polo crosses Mexico, floods U.S. Southwest
science.summary: Hurricane Polo made landfall in Baja California Sur on Tuesday as a Category 2 storm, with maximum sustained winds of 110 mph. It later made a second landfall in Sonora before weakening and dissipating over northwestern Mexico Tuesday night. In Puerto San Carlos, flooding and fallen trees affected streets and homes; ab
science.content: Hurricane Polo made landfall in Baja California Sur on Tuesday as a Category 2 storm, with maximum sustained winds of 110 mph. It later made a second landfall in Sonora before weakening and dissipating over northwestern Mexico Tuesday night. In Puerto San Carlos, flooding and fallen trees affected streets and homes; about 700 people were in shelters, and authorities initially reported no serious damage or deaths in Baja California Sur. Polo’s remnants brought flooding to the U.S. Southwest, where residents in parts of New Mexico evacuated after officials warned that a dam could fail.
science.image_alt: Hurricane Polo crosses Mexico, floods U.S. Southwest

science.title: Nepal rains trigger Kaligandaki landslide, briefly blocking river
science.summary: A large landslide fell into the Kaligandaki River near Lete in Nepal’s Mustang district on Sept. 27, temporarily blocking the river. Landslide researcher Dave Petley said it was difficult to pinpoint the exact site. The landslide occurred during a wider spell of flooding and slope failures across Nepal. The BBC reporte
science.content: A large landslide fell into the Kaligandaki River near Lete in Nepal’s Mustang district on Sept. 27, temporarily blocking the river. Landslide researcher Dave Petley said it was difficult to pinpoint the exact site. The landslide occurred during a wider spell of flooding and slope failures across Nepal. The BBC reported that the country’s disaster agency recorded at least 27 deaths from floods and landslides in recent days; the toll covers the wider disaster, not necessarily the Kaligandaki slide.
science.image_alt: Nepal rains trigger Kaligandaki landslide, briefly blocking river

science.title: Researchers report new solar materials and underwater photovoltaic tests
science.summary: Oregon State University researchers developed a family of materials that use sunlight to produce hydrogen from water, offering a route for converting solar energy into chemical fuel. The article description does not provide efficiency figures or further experimental details. Separately, researchers working near China’s
science.content: Oregon State University researchers developed a family of materials that use sunlight to produce hydrogen from water, offering a route for converting solar energy into chemical fuel. The article description does not provide efficiency figures or further experimental details. Separately, researchers working near China’s Weizhou Island generated electricity from sunlight underwater. Futurism reported that the perovskite-based cells were adjusted to use blue and green light that penetrates the ocean.

sports.summary: Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott was sentenced to seven years in prison at the High Court in Edinburgh on September 29, 2026, after a jury convicted him in August of sexually abusing a girl and a boy. Dott, 49, denied the charges. The offences against the girl occurred from 1993 to 1996, and those against the
sports.content: Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott was sentenced to seven years in prison at the High Court in Edinburgh on September 29, 2026, after a jury convicted him in August of sexually abusing a girl and a boy. Dott, 49, denied the charges. The offences against the girl occurred from 1993 to 1996, and those against the boy from 2006 to 2010. Dott won the world title in 2006. His seven-year sentence was backdated to August 24, when he was taken into custody.
sports.image_alt: Former snooker world champion Graeme Dott jailed for seven years

sports.title: White Sox beat Astros 6-3 in wild-card opener
sports.summary: The Chicago White Sox beat the Houston Astros 6-3 at Daikin Park on Sept. 29 to take a 1-0 lead in their best-of-three American League Wild Card Series. Sam Antonacci drove in two runs with a second-inning single, and Colson Montgomery hit a solo home run as Chicago built an early advantage. It was the White Sox’s firs
sports.content: The Chicago White Sox beat the Houston Astros 6-3 at Daikin Park on Sept. 29 to take a 1-0 lead in their best-of-three American League Wild Card Series. Sam Antonacci drove in two runs with a second-inning single, and Colson Montgomery hit a solo home run as Chicago built an early advantage. It was the White Sox’s first postseason victory since 2021. Chicago returned to the playoffs after three consecutive seasons with at least 100 losses, including a 121-loss campaign in 2024. The White Sox became the first MLB team to reach the postseason after consecutive 100-loss seasons. Houston, which finished 81-81, became the first team to reach the postseason without a winning record.
sports.image_alt: White Sox beat Astros 6-3 in wild-card opener

sports.title: England drop Toone, Kelly for Greece World Cup playoff
sports.summary: England manager Sarina Wiegman left out midfielder Ella Toone and forward Chloe Kelly from her squad for October’s Women’s World Cup qualifying playoff against Greece, saying their recent club performances had not reached the level she expected. Both players were influential in England’s European Championship wins in 2
sports.content: England manager Sarina Wiegman left out midfielder Ella Toone and forward Chloe Kelly from her squad for October’s Women’s World Cup qualifying playoff against Greece, saying their recent club performances had not reached the level she expected. Both players were influential in England’s European Championship wins in 2022 and 2025. England did not secure direct qualification during the group stage after losing to Spain and will seek a place at the 2027 tournament through the playoff. The squad includes the returning Leah Williamson and Chelsea midfielder Lexi Potter, who received her first call-up.
sports.image_alt: England drop Toone, Kelly for Greece World Cup playoff

sports.title: No. 8 New York Liberty sweep top-seeded Lynx 2-0
sports.summary: The New York Liberty beat the Minnesota Lynx 87-71 in Game 2 on Tuesday, completing a 2-0 first-round sweep and advancing to the WNBA semifinals. The No. 8 seed became the first eighth-seeded team to eliminate a No. 1 seed in the league’s 30-year history. New York will face either the Atlanta Dream or Washington Mystic
sports.content: The New York Liberty beat the Minnesota Lynx 87-71 in Game 2 on Tuesday, completing a 2-0 first-round sweep and advancing to the WNBA semifinals. The No. 8 seed became the first eighth-seeded team to eliminate a No. 1 seed in the league’s 30-year history. New York will face either the Atlanta Dream or Washington Mystics in the semifinals; Atlanta leads that series 1-0. The Liberty and Lynx had also met in the 2024 WNBA Finals.
sports.image_alt: No. 8 New York Liberty sweep top-seeded Lynx 2-0

sports.title: USMNT rallies past Chile 4-2 as teenagers set records
sports.summary: The United States came back from 2-1 down to beat Chile 4-2 in a friendly in St. Louis on Tuesday, September 29. Sebastian Berhalter opened the scoring, Julian Hall equalized after Chile moved ahead, Chris Richards put the U.S. in front in the 72nd minute, and Mathis Albert added a stoppage-time goal. Albert, a Borussi
sports.content: The United States came back from 2-1 down to beat Chile 4-2 in a friendly in St. Louis on Tuesday, September 29. Sebastian Berhalter opened the scoring, Julian Hall equalized after Chile moved ahead, Chris Richards put the U.S. in front in the 72nd minute, and Mathis Albert added a stoppage-time goal. Albert, a Borussia Dortmund teenager, scored at 17 years and 131 days to become the youngest scorer in USMNT history, passing Christian Pulisic’s mark; Hall, 18, scored in each of his first two senior appearances. The match ended with two confrontations involving players from both teams.
sports.image_alt: USMNT rallies past Chile 4-2 as teenagers set records

sports.title: Giants release Odell Beckham Jr. after three games
sports.summary: The New York Giants released wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. on September 29, ending his second stint with the team after three games. The 33-year-old returned on a one-year deal after more than a year out of football. He played 20 offensive snaps, received one target and did not make a catch; he was behind Malik Naber
sports.content: The New York Giants released wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. on September 29, ending his second stint with the team after three games. The 33-year-old returned on a one-year deal after more than a year out of football. He played 20 offensive snaps, received one target and did not make a catch; he was behind Malik Nabers, Darnell Mooney and Malachi Fields on the depth chart. The Giants and Beckham mutually agreed to part ways, allowing him to seek a team where he could play more. The Giants signed him in June and placed him on their 53-man roster, but his role remained limited through the opening three games.
sports.image_alt: Giants release Odell Beckham Jr. after three games

sports.title: Ferrari backs F1 chief Vasseur after Horner job speculation
sports.summary: Ferrari said on September 29 that it remained confident in Frederic Vasseur and his team, adding that its position had not changed. Chief communications officer Maria Conti made the statement on behalf of chairman John Elkann and CEO Benedetto Vigna during an unscheduled media call. The announcement followed former Red
sports.content: Ferrari said on September 29 that it remained confident in Frederic Vasseur and his team, adding that its position had not changed. Chief communications officer Maria Conti made the statement on behalf of chairman John Elkann and CEO Benedetto Vigna during an unscheduled media call. The announcement followed former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner’s comments in an interview with The Times that leading Ferrari would be his “dream” job, prompting speculation that he could replace Vasseur.
sports.image_alt: Ferrari backs F1 chief Vasseur after Horner job speculation

sports.title: Bears
sports.summary: Chicago Bears third-string quarterback Case Keenum led a 27-7 win over the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field on Monday, September 28. In his first NFL regular-season appearance in 1,009 days, the 38-year-old completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and two touchdowns and scored on a one-yard run. The win improved Chi
sports.content: Chicago Bears third-string quarterback Case Keenum led a 27-7 win over the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field on Monday, September 28. In his first NFL regular-season appearance in 1,009 days, the 38-year-old completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and two touchdowns and scored on a one-yard run. The win improved Chicago to 2-1 and handed Philadelphia its first loss of the season. Keenum started after Caleb Williams, Chicago's starting quarterback, injured his hamstring in the previous game and backup Tyson Bagent suffered a concussion. Bagent was cleared, but Keenum took first-team reps during the week.
